title: Activation signal synthesis and ops decision log (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for how we synthesize heterogeneous signals (metrics, model-quality probes, safety heuristics, human-review samplers) into automated canary gating and operator-facing decision prompts during cross-functional rollouts and A/B experiments. The goal: reduce cognitive load for stewards, make rollback/fallback decisions auditable, and enable faster safe launches for LLM behaviors.

Context / motivation (why this is slightly different):
- We keep seeing noise from correlated telemetry (latency spikes + traffic changes) and ops people making different decisions across releases. Need a compact signal synthesis pattern that (a) distinguishes infrastructure regressions from model-behavior regressions, and (b) surfaces small-sample-high-concern cases for human triage.
- This doc sits between: the lower-level signal catalog (Confluence) and the rollout playbooks. Think of it as the "decision log" scaffolding that a steward fills during an activation.

Open questions (notes to self):
- How strict should multi-signal gating be when slices conflict? e.g., latency OK but QA-sample failure rate 0.4% — do we pause at 0.2%? Need product tolerance input.
- We need a canonical mapping of detection->remediation (auto-fallback to smaller model / increase batch-size / route to dedicated capacity). Who owns that mapping? Ops or serving-runtime?

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- Activation steward: owns the decision log, triggers and reviews canary observations, coordinates cross-functional comms.
- Oncall SRE: investigates infra anomalies (latency, memory OOMs, infra-level errors).
- Model owner / applied ML: interprets model-quality probes, triages sample failures and provides quick mitigations (prompt tweak, soften temperature, switch model variant).
- Product PM / Launch owner: decides exposure progression and customer communications.

Signal taxonomy (synthesis inputs):
1) Infrastructure signals (automated): p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate (5xx, 4xx), GPU memory pressure, queue length, autoscaler events. Thresholds numeric + directionality.
2) Business signals (automated): conversion click-through, payment-authorize errors, upstream API failures. Often lagging; lower weight for immediate gating.
3) Model-quality probes (automated): eval-suite pass rate, prompt-specific metrics (hallucination flags, incorrect entity extraction), embedding drift score.
4) Human-review samples (semi-automated): curated sample queue where reviewers tag severity.
5) Safety heuristics (automated & ML): toxicity classifier spike, sensitive-entity hits, legal/regulatory keywords.
6) Observability annotations (manual): deployment notes, config changes, tests run before activation.

Signal weighting heuristic (SIMPLE first-pass):
- Hard blockers (immediate halt): infra 5xx>0.5% AND p99 latency > 3x baseline AND GPU OOMs observed; OR safety heuristic spike > configured stop threshold (default 0.1% of traffic with high-severity hits).
- High-risk model signals (pause + human triage): model-quality probe failure rate > 0.25% OR >3 high-severity human tags in 1k samples.
- Soft anomalies (observe, delay next step): small deviations in p95 (10–25%), or business signals with no prior correlation.
- Persistent drift (escalate): gradual drift in embedding cosine distribution over 24h rolling window (>2 sigma).

Decision synthesis flow (ops-friendly):
1) Ingest live signals into a small decision engine (can be a rule graph + score).
2) Produce a single composite "activation_health" status: green / amber / red, with contributing reasons and a short action suggestion.
3) If red -> auto-fallback (if configured) and create an incident ticket + send activation-steward + oncall SRE. If amber -> hold progression and send summary to steward for manual continue/stop.

Suggested composite scoring (skeletal):
- activation_health_score = w_infra*infra_score + w_model*model_score + w_safety*safety_score + w_human*human_score
- Default weights (starting): w_infra=0.35, w_model=0.35, w_safety=0.2, w_human=0.1.
- Scores normalized 0..1 where 1 == healthy. Map to green if score>0.9, amber 0.7-0.9, red <0.7.
- NOTE: weights should be configurable per-experiment/feature. For safety-sensitive features, increase w_safety to 0.5.

Pseudocode for gating rule (working):
- // called every minute by rollout controller
- read latest_metrics for slice S
- infra_ok = (p99<S.p99_threshold && error_rate<S.error_threshold && gpu_ooms==0)
- model_ok = (probe_fail_rate<S.model_fail_threshold)
- safety_ok = (safety_spike_rate<S.safety_stop_threshold)
- human_alerts = recent_human_tags(S, window=1000)
- composite = weighted_score(infra_ok, model_ok, safety_ok, human_alerts)
- if composite<0.7: set activation_health=red; if auto_fallback_enabled: trigger_fallback()
- else if composite<0.9: activation_health=amber; notify_steward()
- else activation_health=green; continue_progression()

Slice selection & cohort heuristics (practical tips):
- Small-batch escape hatch: always include a 0.01% global traffic micro-slice seeded with synthetic adversarial prompts (high-sensitivity). This helps early safety detection without impacting users.
- Orthogonal slices: choose slices that are orthogonal in risk (e.g., region x device type x user-experience flow). Avoid overlapping slices that will muddy attribution.
- Progressive amplification: start with low exposure for highest-risk slices and mirror the normal traffic mix as we expand.

Comms / cadence during a staged rollout:
- Pre-activation: publish an "activation snapshot" to #rollout-ops with model version, expected SLOs, risk profile, and decision mapping. Attach the decision log URL.
- Minute-0..30: steward posts 5-min cadence updates (first 3 updates automated).
- On amber/red: steward runs quick triage and writes decision entry (reason, actions taken, link to sample IDs).
- Post-activation: fill the final decision log entry, link to incident/rollforward PR, and tag product + applied-ml owners.

Decision log template (one-line fields for quick filling):
- activation_id: (generated)
- steward: (name)
- start_time: (ISO)
- slices_active: (list)
- activation_health: (green/amber/red)
- contributing_signals: (short bullets)
- human_samples_flagged: (n / ids)
- action_taken: (auto-fallback / hold / rollback / proceed)
- rationale: (1-2 lines)
- followup_owner: (name + ticket)

Playbook for common scenarios (ops-first checklist):
- scenario: sudden p99 spike but no model probe failures
  - check autoscaler logs, queue length, infra alerts
  - if infra issue confirmed -> pause canary expansion, notify SRE, do not rollback model yet
  - if infra nominal -> promote amber -> human-sample check for correlated tokenization issues
- scenario: safety-spike detected in micro-slice
  - immediately set activation_health=red, capture top 20 samples, route to safety-reviewers
  - enable auto-fallback (route to safe-model variant) and stop further expansion
- scenario: model-quality probe increases gradually during expansion
  - slow progression, increase human sampling rate, consider reweighting probes to be stricter

Unresolved operational items (for follow-up):
- Need a lightweight UI for the steward to sign-off amber -> green transitions (current console flow is too many clicks).
- Correlate sample IDs across telemetry and human-review queues (investigate storage/indexing options).
- Define per-product default weights and stop thresholds (ask PMs for tolerance matrix).

Appendix: quick links and artifacts to copy into formal runbook later:
- Signal catalog (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ROLL/Signal+Catalog
- Activation decision schema (proto): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/789
- Example incident ticket: PROD-3421

Notes to reviewer: feel free to paste this into the rollout runbook as a "decision-log pattern" section. This is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight; we can iterate after a few activations.

---
End of working draft.
